title: Shared filesystem, JSON, and report-writing helper family
problemStatement: Low-level JSON config loading and report emission were repeatedly hand-rolled across the usr CI gates and multiple parity/smoke tests with the same mkdir+JSON.stringify+newline+writeFile sequence and repeated JSON.parse(readFile()) helpers. Those call sites were small but numerous, making changes to formatting or directory-creation behavior noisy and inconsistent.

duplicateClusters.name: USR guardrail scripts reading config and writing JSON reports
duplicateClusters.bestFix: Use one shared async JSON file helper for config loads and report writes so the gates stop duplicating directory creation and pretty-print rules.

duplicateClusters.name: Parity and smoke tests with bespoke JSON fixture/report writers
duplicateClusters.bestFix: Replace local helpers with the same shared JSON read/write module where the behavior is generic and not artifact-specific.

whyCurrentSharedModulesWereInsufficient: src/shared/files.js includes safe JSON reads for specific consumers, but not a small general-purpose async read/write helper for ordinary config and report files.
src/shared/json-stream.js is oriented around artifact and JSONL emission rather than ordinary JSON file persistence.
